The Cass County Auditor-Treasurer collects the tax at the courthouse, 303 Minnesota Avenue W, second floor, in Walker. Phone (218) 547-7260 and mail to PO Box 3000, Walker, MN 56484. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm. Besides property tax, the department runs elections, vital statistics, licensing and the parcel mapping system.

Value and classification belong to the county assessor at (218) 547-7298. Valuation runs through a single county-wide system, so one office values every township parcel and no local assessors are involved. Staff appraisers view each property about once every five years and look at all new construction and alterations in the current year.

The first half of real property tax is due May 15, and the non-farm second half is due October 15. Farm real property and manufactured homes pay their second half on November 15. A deadline that falls on a weekend or legal holiday slides to the next business day, and personal property taxes share the real property schedule.

Cass County tax due dates by property type
Due dateProperty and installment
May 15Real property, first half (or the whole bill if it is $100 or less)
May 31Resorts, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first half (or all if $50 or less)
October 15Non-farm real property, second half
November 15Farm real property and manufactured homes, second half

The May 31 resort date comes from Minn. Stat. 279.01. It extends the date to commercial seasonal recreational property in classes 1c and 4c and to class 3a property that earns over 60 percent of its gross income in May through August. A class 3a owner attaches an affidavit, and the county asks eligible businesses to return its Commercial Tax Deferral Form.

The county's payment page lists these routes:

  • At the courthouse during office hours.
  • By mail to the Cass County Auditor-Treasurer with the right stub, postmarked before the due date. The second-half stub sits directly above the first-half stub at the bottom of the statement.
  • Autopay through MuniciPay. An ACH payment costs $1.00 and a card costs 2.25% of the payment with a $1.00 minimum.
  • By phone at (218) 321-9802, with a confirmation number noted down.
  • Through a mortgage escrow account. If a lender pays the bill, your statement copy says that taxes paid by an escrow agent should not be paid again.

Electronic payments take about two business days to post, so do not wait for the due date. Near a deadline, ask the local postmaster to hand-stamp a mailed envelope. Fees on electronic payments go to the service provider, not the county.

Improved parcels here carry a flat refuse management fee when assessed value is at least $1,000. The charge began in 1990, was once called the solid waste fee, and funds waste disposal and recycling programs. The county board has kept it as a flat fee instead of folding the cost into the levy.

  • Residential and seasonal properties: $86
  • Commercial under $9,999 in building value: $86
  • Commercial from $10,000 to $99,999: $195
  • Commercial from $100,000 to $499,999: $391
  • Commercial at $500,000 and up: $652
  • Apartments: $16 per unit
  • Non-commercial tax-exempt buildings: $86

Any improved parcel you sell will carry this line, so the buyer's first bill includes it.

The notice of assessed value mailed each spring explains how to appeal. The assessor's office answers questions all year at (218) 547-7298. Local boards of appeal sit between April 1 and May 31 under Minn. Stat. 274.01, and anyone who is told of a proposed increase and fails to show up or write in may not go on to the county board.

Market value is set as of January 2 each year. The state expects an assessor's value to land between 90% and 105% of sale price. File a homestead application with the assessor. The same office can tell blind or disabled owners whether they qualify for the relief Minnesota offers them. The state runs the refund program for homeowners, so use the Department of Revenue forms and instructions for those questions.

Give the Auditor-Treasurer your new mailing address the day you move. A wrong address can delay or block time-sensitive statements and other property mailings, and care-of addresses can be added. No owner name is changed in the tax records without a recorded legal document.

A short checklist before you list: find your most recent statement and both stubs, confirm the class printed on it, ask the assessor to confirm your homestead status, and note the refuse fee amount. Having these ready also makes it easy for a buyer, a lender or a cash buyer's title company to verify the parcel and set the closing figures.

If you are working through a contract for deed, read the county's Property Tax Billing and Collection Procedures fact sheet, which explains who receives the statement.

Before closing, ask the Auditor-Treasurer for the balance on the parcel, including the refuse fee line. A cash sale skips the lender, so the title company will settle the tax from your proceeds at the table.

Interest begins on unpaid balances after January 2 of the following year, and penalties and rates follow state statute. Partial payments are accepted on prior-year taxes, with a $100 minimum preferred. The money goes to the newest year first and then back through earlier years. Nonpayment can end in loss of the property through forfeiture under Minnesota law.

Call the Auditor-Treasurer at (218) 547-7260 for the amount past due on a parcel, and ask for the figure as of your expected closing date. If you sell on a contract for deed, only the new contract holder receives the bill, but you still have to watch that the taxes get paid.

Cass County is large and quiet. It has 2,022 square miles of land, a population of 31,430, and 25,344 housing units against 12,874 households, which points to a large stock of seasonal and second homes. Walker holds the courthouse, and Lake Shore is the biggest city. Median owner-occupied home value is $288,300.

Class 4c seasonal recreational property takes the homestead penalty schedule. If you are listing a lake cabin in a township such as Pine River, Shingobee or Boy Lake, check the class on the statement and the payment dates that go with it.

faqs.q: What are the Cass County payment deadlines?
faqs.a: May 15 for the first half of real property and October 15 for the second half of non-farm property. Farm real property and manufactured homes pay the second half on November 15, and resorts have until May 31.

faqs.q: Can I pay Cass County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, through MuniciPay. ACH costs $1.00 per payment and a debit or credit card costs 2.25% with a $1.00 minimum. Allow two business days for posting.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Cass County tax payment?
faqs.a: Send it to the Cass County Auditor-Treasurer, PO Box 3000, Walker, MN 56484, with the stub from your statement, or bring it to the courthouse at 303 Minnesota Avenue W.

faqs.q: What is the $86 charge on a Cass County tax statement?
faqs.a: It is the refuse management fee that applies to residential and seasonal parcels with an assessed value of at least $1,000. It pays for waste disposal and recycling in the county.

faqs.q: Who decides my Cass County homestead status?
faqs.a: The Cass County Assessor's Office reviews homestead applications. Call (218) 547-7298 to apply or to check the status.
